solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Dailies in a frenzy about Labour's "last" PM

indicators.note: letters in a frenzy are thrown wildly about, so this word gets reshuffled
about means surrounding, so the reshuffled letters wrap round the next piece

explanation.surface: The tabloids go wild over the most recent Labour prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around "last" hint that it is not about recent history at all: it takes the final letter, which the rearranged letters wrap round.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli was a Victorian Conservative prime minister, so he is an example of a PM.

clue.text: Balls, say, hoisted on tortured inmate by part of Bible – a function of Guantanamo Bay

indicators.note: in a down clue, hoisting lifts the letters so they read from bottom to top
something tortured is twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: Ed Balls, the Labour politician, is an example of an Ed

explanation.surface: A satirical jab at the US prison camp, with a crude double meaning in Balls and a tortured inmate.
explanation.walkthrough: Balls looks like a rude noun but is the surname of the Labour politician Ed Balls; ED goes up to DE. DE + TAINME + NT gives DETAINMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Guantanamo Bay is a US camp whose purpose is holding prisoners, so confinement is what it serves to do.

clue.text: Cameron's lead snatched by "festering non-believer"

indicators.note: a word's lead is its opening letter, the one at the front
something snatched is held inside the grabber, so one piece goes within the other

explanation.surface: David Cameron's leadership seized by a rotten unbeliever, perhaps a Eurosceptic rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside SEPTIC to give SCEPTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptic doubts or rejects accepted beliefs, so the word is a synonym for a doubter.

clue.text: Partner of old queen has bishop inside with it

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other word

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
someone with it is sharp and alert

explanation.surface: An old queen's companion keeps a bishop in his house and is fashionably up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: B goes inside ALERT: AL-B-ERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Albert was the husband and consort of Queen Victoria, so he is her partner.

clue.text: Willy cramps at centre for cycling wear?

indicators.note: at centre says the letters sit in the middle of the words given, running across them

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words, inside

explanation.surface: A cramped willy is what you get from tight cycling shorts.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the definition by example: not all cycling wear is LYCRA, but much of it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra is a stretchy synthetic fabric used for tight cyclists' shorts and jerseys.

clue.text: Falsely shy, etc., like Jordan?

indicators.note: what is put falsely is misrepresented, so these letters appear in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Is the glamour model only pretending to be bashful?
explanation.walkthrough: Jordan was the stage name of Katie Price, a British glamour model known for her large breasts; the question mark admits the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Chesty means big-bosomed, the trait for which that model was famous.

clue.text: "Oh to roll over on Boris's backside!", Ms Ford's joyous cries

indicators.note: rolling over turns the word upside down, so in this down entry it reads backwards
the backside of a word is its tail end, its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned round
Anna Ford, the British TV newsreader, with the possessive

explanation.surface: A newsreader exclaims with delight about rolling on top of Boris Johnson's bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: Anna Ford was a well-known BBC and ITN newsreader. HO + S + ANNAS gives HOSANNAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosannas are shouts of praise and adoration, originally liturgical, so they are exultant cries.

clue.text: Sun destroyed expert

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for Sunday, or the sun

explanation.surface: The Sun newspaper wrecked a specialist's reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled worker is accomplished and proficient, the adjectival sense of expert.

clue.text: Gay movement's about love, mind, body discipline

indicators.note: a movement shifts things around, so these letters move into another order
about means around, so the shifted letters go round the next piece

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: The gay rights movement is all about love, and a holistic outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: Love as O comes from tennis scoring, where love means nil.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoga is a Hindu-derived practice of postures and breathing that trains mental and physical control together.

clue.text: Nil perks! Tricky to make a splash

indicators.note: something tricky is devious and twisted, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: No job benefits makes it hard to stand out from the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Make a splash usually means attract attention; here it is taken literally, scattering drops of liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprinkle is to scatter small drops of water over something, literally splashing it.

clue.text: (& 26ac.) Ragman's article put by blue JCB?

blocks.note: a JCB is a British brand of mechanical digger

explanation.surface: A rag-and-bone man's goods are set beside a sad-looking excavator.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye has long called the press baron Rupert Murdoch the Dirty Digger, digger being Australian slang for an Australian. A rag is a tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Murdoch owns newspapers that Private Eye calls rags, so this nickname names a tabloid proprietor.

clue.text: Dollar spending is avoiding responsibility

blocks.note: a buck is informal for a dollar

explanation.surface: Splashing out cash is a way of dodging what you owe.
explanation.walkthrough: Spending suggests money, given the dollar, but here it is spending time.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing the buck is the idiom for shifting blame or duty onto someone else.

clue.text: see 20ac.
Palin's first regular nightclub engagement? Palin's dream!

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: a performer's residency is a regular booking at one venue

explanation.surface: Sarah Palin dreams of a regular slot in a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: Sarah Palin, the 2008 US vice-presidential candidate, had hopes of the White House.
explanation.definitionFit: Palin aspired to the US presidency, so the office is her ambition.

clue.text: Shit MP's chief Conservative to break the country

indicators.note: the chief letter of a word is its leading one
breaking into something means getting inside it

explanation.surface: A dodgy MP's Tory leader is set to wreck Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside UK, and M goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Muck is dirt or dung, a milder word for excrement.

clue.text: Court sort of strike against Brenda's shameful payout

blocks.note: a tennis stroke played on a court
Private Eye calls the Queen Brenda; ER is the royal cipher

explanation.surface: A court case about some industrial action involving the Queen's disgraceful settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: Court and strike suggest a legal or labour dispute; they are tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: A backhander is slang for a bribe, an illicit payment slipped to someone.

clue.text: Yen to be hugged by arse-like relative causes breakdown

indicators.note: what is hugged is held inside the arms of another, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: Y is the abbreviation for yen, the Japanese currency

explanation.surface: A craving to be embraced by an uptight family member brings on a collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: Breakdown looks like a nervous collapse, but it is the sense of itemising. The relative is a two-part piece, so the yen sits between its halves.
explanation.definitionFit: An analysis is a detailed breakdown, separating something into its component parts.

clue.text: Snotrag inside out – perverted token of gratitude

indicators.note: inside places one piece within another
perverted means twisted out of its proper form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a handkerchief, crudely called a snotrag

explanation.surface: A soiled handkerchief turned inside out makes a twisted gift of thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside out looks like one phrase; split it, so the snotrag goes inside the other word once that is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying the phrase is the verbal expression of thanks, a small sign of appreciation.

clue.text: Half the country's thrown off by beer

indicators.note: thrown off means knocked out of place, so these letters get muddled

explanation.surface: Half the nation is knocked off balance by drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The country is Wales, whose northern part is roughly half of it.
explanation.definitionFit: North Wales is the northern region of Wales, roughly one half of that nation.

clue.text: Brenda's upset on account of M&S alterations

indicators.note: upset tips something over, so in this down entry the letters read upwards

blocks.note: Private Eye calls the Queen Brenda; ER is her cipher
the letters of Marks & Spencer's short name

explanation.surface: The Queen is unhappy about the changes at Marks & Spencer, the British high-street store.
explanation.walkthrough: RE + FOR + MS gives REFORMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Reforms are changes made to improve something, so they are modifications.

clue.text: (& 12ac.) 10/26's outfit shows anal retention wins out

indicators.note: out here means disordered or wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Murdoch's company proves that obsessive control pays off.
explanation.walkthrough: 10/26 refers to the answer at 10 and 26 across, Rupert Murdoch's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: News International was Murdoch's British newspaper company, publishing The Sun and The Times.

clue.text: Hopping because of kinky gear stuck in arse

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so these letters are rearranged
stuck in places one piece inside another

explanation.surface: Someone hopping about after fetish kit gets lodged somewhere painful.
explanation.walkthrough: Hopping looks like jumping about in pain; it is hopping mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopping, as in hopping mad, is informal for extremely angry.

clue.text: Web's originator wearing suit! Get off line!

indicators.note: the originator of a word is the letter it starts from
the piece wearing a garment is inside it

blocks.note: to suit a purpose is to serve it

explanation.surface: Tim Berners-Lee in a business suit is told to log off the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: Web's originator suggests Tim Berners-Lee and get off line suggests going offline; the line is a road lane.
explanation.definitionFit: To swerve is to veer suddenly off a straight course or out of one's lane.

clue.text: "Rich Europe in America's eyes" laughed at by Eye readers

blocks.note: Americans call Europe the Old World

explanation.surface: The magazine's readers mock the American view of wealthy Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Funny Old World is a long-running Private Eye column of odd news stories, so its readers laugh at it.
explanation.definitionFit: The column in the magazine collects bizarre reports for readers' amusement.

clue.text: What Brenda is: up for a drink

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: Brenda is Private Eye's name for the Queen, who is royal

explanation.surface: The Queen is keen on a drink, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: REGAL read upwards gives LAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light, fizzy beer, so it is one kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Maybe Ant's missus goes topless

indicators.note: going topless loses what is on top, here the opening letter of a down entry

blocks.note: madam is the formal address for a woman, as missus is the informal one

explanation.surface: The wife of the comedian Ant goes bare-chested, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant suggests Ant McPartlin of Ant and Dec; it is the 1980s pop star Adam Ant, so the definition is his first name, with maybe for the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam Ant's forename is Adam, so this is the name that might go with Ant.

clue.text: see 10ac.
One breaking the extremes of Gordon's spirit

indicators.note: breaking into something gets inside it
the extremes of a word are its two outermost letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of Gordon

explanation.surface: Someone shatters Gordon Brown's morale.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon's is also a famous gin brand, which makes the surface apt. I goes inside GN.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin is a juniper-flavoured distilled liquor, one of the spirits.

clue.text: Cyclops rejected cat fluff

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the setter, Cyclops, refers to themself

explanation.surface: The setter turned down some cat hair.
explanation.walkthrough: Fluff looks like fur; it is the verb meaning to bungle.
explanation.definitionFit: To fluff a task is to botch it, which is what a mess-up does.

clue.text: One arse long cherished by Twitterer, "Matey"

indicators.note: what is cherished is held close, so these pieces sit inside the other

blocks.note: Stephen Fry, the British comedian, was a famously prolific Twitter user
L is the abbreviation for long

explanation.surface: A tweeter keeps a long-loved backside close, calling it mate.
explanation.walkthrough: Long-cherished reads as one phrase, but long is a separate piece and cherished signals the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Matey describes someone sociable and familiar, an informal synonym for amiable.
